Create an ir Header to Reproduce Reactives

Source: R/reprex_header.R
reprex_header.Rd

Capture the exact package versions, R version and a dependency snapshot date needed to reproduce one or more shiny::reactive objects, as a single ir header. Prepending the header to the script returned by reprex_reactive() lets the recipient run ir run script.R with no separate lockfile or project to share.

Snapshot Scope

As with reprex_lockfile(), the package versions pinned are read from the currently loaded library (.libPaths()), so they match the running Shiny session that produced the reactives.

Usage

reprex_header(
  ...,
  packages = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  r_version = TRUE,
  exclude_newer = Sys.Date(),
  isolated = TRUE,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

...

One or more shiny::reactive objects to reproduce. If none are supplied, every reactive registered by register_reactives() is used, so a modular application can offer a whole-app header without threading reactives up to the top level.

packages

Character vector of package names to pin. If NULL (the default), every package detected across ... is used. Supplying this lets the user narrow the set, or add a package the detector could not find (for example one attached only for an operator or method).

exclude

Character vector of package names to omit from the header.

r_version

Whether to pin the R version the script was generated under. TRUE (the default) pins the running getRversion() exactly; FALSE omits the r-version field; a string is used as-is, for example ">= 4.3" to require a minimum rather than an exact version.

exclude_newer

A Date, or a string coercible to one, naming the Posit Package Manager snapshot ir resolves dependencies against. Defaults to today, so dependencies are fixed as of the day the header is created.

isolated

Whether ir installs packages into an isolated, per-script library rather than reusing packages already available. Defaults to TRUE.

session

The Shiny session to read registered reactives from. Only used when ... is empty and packages is NULL.

Value

A single string holding the ir header, including a trailing newline, ready to be pasted above the output of reprex_reactive().

See also

reprex_packages() to inspect the detected set without building a header, reprex_lockfile() for a whole-project renv lockfile, and register_reactives() to record reactives from within each module.

Examples

library(shiny)

numeric_iris <- reactive(purrr::keep(iris, is.numeric))

# Outside a running application, isolate supplies the reactive context
isolate(cat(reprex_header(numeric_iris, exclude_newer = "2025-05-15")))
#> #!/usr/bin/env -S ir run
#> #| packages:
#> #|   - purrr==1.2.2
#> #| r-version: "==4.6.2"
#> #| isolated: true
#> #| exclude-newer: "2025-05-15"
